def post_refund(journal: Journal, refund_id: str, order_id: str, goods_cents: int, tax_cents: int,
                shipping_cents: int, posted: date, *, to_store_credit: bool = False) -> Entry:
    """Refund: contra-revenue for goods and shipping, the tax given back reduces tax payable. Paid back
    to the card, or as store credit when the customer chose that."""
    total = goods_cents + tax_cents + shipping_cents
    lines = [
        dr(A.REFUNDS, goods_cents + shipping_cents),
        dr(A.SALES_TAX_PAYABLE, tax_cents),
        cr(A.CUSTOMER_CREDIT if to_store_credit else A.CASH_CLEARING, total),
    ]
    return journal.post(posted, f"Refund {refund_id} for {order_id}", lines, source="refund", source_ref=refund_id)

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence

from shopkit.warehouse.sites import Lot, Site, SiteStock
from shopkit.warehouse.waves import EXPRESS, STANDARD, WaveOrder, allocate_wave


@dataclass
class _CartLine:
    """One line of a cart, expressed as a (sku, qty) pair for the wave allocator."""
    sku: str
    qty: int = 1


@dataclass
class _CartOrder:
    """A synthetic order carrying the cart's SKUs so the wave allocator can be exercised."""
    id: str = "CART"
    lines: list[_CartLine] = field(default_factory=list)


def _wave_orders_for(cart: _CartOrder, service: str) -> list:
    """Build a :class:`~shopkit.warehouse.waves.WaveOrder` for each line of the cart, asking the
    allocator to use *service*.  One line per call keeps each SKU's stock demand independent of the
    others so a shortage in one SKU does not hide that another SKU *could* ship by express."""
    orders = []
    for line in cart.lines:
        # WaveOrder.order is typed as Order; duck-typing lets us pass our lightweight cart object
        # without importing the full order model.
        orders.append(
            WaveOrder(
                order=_OrderLike(cart.id, line.sku, line.qty),
                service=service,
                paid_at=None,
                country="US",
                gift=False,
                hold="",
            )
        )
    return orders


@dataclass
class _OrderLike:
    """Minimal stand-in for :class:`shopkit.orders.models.Order` accepted by the allocator."""
    id: str
    sku: str
    qty: int
    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)
    gift: bool = False
    total: int = 0


def express_available(
    skus: Sequence[str],
    sites: Sequence[Site],
    hazmat_skus: frozenset[str] | set[str] | None,
    *,
    stock: SiteStock | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """Return True when the warehouse would put an order containing *skus* into an express wave.

    The answer is based on the real allocation engine: it asks the same allocator used for live
    waves whether every requested SKU can be covered by sites that offer the ``express`` service.
    A hazmat SKU disqualifies any site whose service set does not include ``express`` for that SKU, so
    the combined demand of hazmat and non-hazmat SKUs must all be satisfiable on express-capable
    sites for the flag to be True.

    Parameters
    ----------
    skus:
        Cart SKUs, one per unit requested (duplicates count as multiple units).
    sites:
        Warehouse sites that could ship the order.
    hazmat_skus:
        SKUs classed as dangerous goods.  Express is never offered for these; they can only be
        shipped from ground sites, which removes any express capacity for those units.
    stock:
        Optional :class:`~shopkit.warehouse.sites.SiteStock` used to check availability.  When
        omitted, the function degrades to a capability check (every non-hazmat SKU must have at
        least one express-capable site in *sites*) and skips the allocation pass.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True when every unit of the cart can be placed on an express wave; False otherwise.
    """
    if not skus:
        return False

    if hazmat_skus is None:
        hazmat_skus = frozenset()

    if not sites:
        return False

    express_sites = [s for s in sites if EXPRESS in s.services]
    if not express_sites:
        return False

    # Count units per SKU; hazmat units must come from non-express-capable sites so they never
    # ride in an express wave.  If the cart has only hazmat SKUs there is nothing to put on an
    # express wave.
    counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    for sku in skus:
        counts[sku] += 1

    hazmat_units = sum(q for sku, q in counts.items() if sku in hazmat_skus)
    non_hazmat_units = sum(q for sku, q in counts.items() if sku not in hazmat_skus)

    if non_hazmat_units == 0:
        # Nothing express-eligible in the cart.
        return False

    if stock is None:
        # Capability-only check: every non-hazmat SKU must be shippable from at least one
        # express-capable site.
        return all(any(sku in _site_skus(s, stock) for s in express_sites) for sku, q in counts.items() if sku not in hazmat_skus)

    # Allocation-based check: run the wave allocator with EXPRESS and confirm no backorder.
    cart = _CartOrder(id="CART", lines=[_CartLine(sku=sku, qty=qty) for sku, qty in counts.items()])
    orders = _wave_orders_for(cart, EXPRESS)
    result = allocate_wave(
        orders,
        list(sites),
        stock,
        today=None,
        hazmat_skus=frozenset(hazmat_skus),
    )
    # Express is available only when every requested SKU was allocated (no backorder entries).
    return not result.backordered


def _site_skus(site: Site, stock: SiteStock | None) -> set[str]:
    """Return the set of SKUs stocked at *site* according to *stock* (empty when no stock)."""
    if stock is None:
        return set()
    return {lot.sku for lot in stock.lots if lot.site == site.code and lot.qty > 0}
